items.followUp: How are elements assigned to the s-, p-, d- or f-block of the modern periodic table?

rubric.why: Block classification is based on the subshell receiving the differentiating (last) electron.
rubric.description: States the basis for dividing elements into blocks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the block to the subshell into which the last electron enters.

rubric.why: These are the four blocks of the modern periodic table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying all four blocks.

modelAnswer: Blocks are divisions of the modern periodic table based on the subshell into which the last electron of an atom enters.
The four blocks are s-block, p-block, d-block and f-block.

items.followUp: What is shielding effect, and how does it affect the effective nuclear charge experienced by an outer electron?

rubric.why: Effective nuclear charge is the net positive charge experienced by an electron in an atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the net positive charge experienced by an electron.

rubric.why: Inner-shell electrons shield an outer electron, so it experiences less than the full nuclear charge.
rubric.description: Explains why the effective nuclear charge is less than the total nuclear charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating the reduction to shielding by inner electrons.

modelAnswer: Effective nuclear charge is the net positive charge experienced by an electron in an atom.
It is less than the total nuclear charge because inner-shell electrons shield the outer electron from the nucleus.

items.followUp: How does heating a liquid affect the kinetic energy of its molecules and its rate of evaporation?

rubric.why: A higher temperature means the liquid molecules have greater kinetic energy.
rubric.description: States that liquid molecules have greater kinetic energy at higher temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the increase in molecular kinetic energy.

rubric.why: More molecules escape into the vapour phase, increasing the vapour pressure.
rubric.description: Links the escape of more molecules to the increase in vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that more molecules escape and the vapour pressure rises.

modelAnswer: At higher temperature, liquid molecules have greater kinetic energy.
More molecules can overcome intermolecular attractions and escape into the vapour phase.
The increased number of vapour molecules produces a higher vapour pressure.

items.followUp: Define molarity and calculate the molarity of a solution containing 0.5 mol of solute in 250 cm³ of solution.

rubric.why: Molarity is the number of moles of solute per unit volume of solution, usually expressed per dm³ or litre.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that molarity is moles of solute per dm³ (or litre) of solution.

rubric.why: The formula expresses molarity as the number of moles divided by the volume of solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the formula M = n/V.

modelAnswer: Molarity is the number of moles of solute dissolved per dm³ (or litre) of solution.
M = n/V, where n is the number of moles of solute and V is the volume of solution in dm³.
The unit of molarity is mol dm⁻³ (or mol L⁻¹).
